title: Book Allocation Problem
problemStatement: Allocate contiguous books to m students so that the maximum pages assigned to any student is minimised.
intuition: The answer lies between max(pages) (one book must fit) and sum(pages) (one student takes all). Greedy chunking tests any candidate maximum in O(n).

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search on the maximum load
approaches.idea: Count students needed for a given cap; shrink the cap while feasible.
approaches.dryRun:
pages=[12,34,67,90] m=2, range [90,203]
cap=146 -> 2 students feasible, hi=146
cap=118 -> 2 feasible
cap=104 -> 3 infeasible
cap=113 -> 2 feasible -> 113
approaches.whyWorks: Greedy filling uses the fewest students for a fixed cap, so it is an exact feasibility test.

interviewInsight: The contiguity constraint is what makes the greedy check valid — say so explicitly.
